title: Turrones de casuy
intro: A soft, sweet cashew paste shaped into little bars and wrapped in thin wafer (ostia) and paper. It tastes like a rich cashew marzipan.

items.name: small sheets of colored paper or cellophane

steps.text: Grind the cashews in a food processor until very fine, stopping before they turn into butter.
Boil the sugar and water in a heavy pan without stirring until a drop in cold water forms a soft ball (about 240°F / 115°C).
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the ground cashews, then the yolks, mixing fast so the yolks do not set in lumps.
Return to low heat and cook, stirring constantly, until the paste is thick and pulls away from the pan.
Spread the paste on a plate and let it cool until it can be handled.
Shape teaspoons of paste into small flat bars, lay each on a piece of wafer and fold or top with a second piece.
Wrap each piece in paper or cellophane and twist the ends.

tips: Ostia is sold in baking supply stores; work with dry hands, because it softens and tears when it touches moisture. Keeps 1 week in an airtight container.

title: Tibok-tibok
intro: A soft, wobbly milk pudding made with carabao milk and topped with golden coconut curds (latik) and lime zest. It is milky, gently sweet and fragrant.

steps.text: Simmer the coconut cream in a pan over medium heat, stirring now and then, until the oil separates and the curds turn golden brown. Strain, keeping the curds and the oil separately.
Brush an 8-inch pan or 2 llaneras with some of the coconut oil.
Whisk the milk, sugar and cornstarch in a pot until smooth, before turning on the heat.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until thick and glossy and big bubbles rise slowly and pop. Stir in half the zest.
Pour into the pan, smooth the top and let it cool and set.
Scatter the latik and the rest of the zest over the top and cut into squares.

tips: With cow's milk, use 3 cups milk and 1 cup evaporated milk for a richer pudding. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge for 2 days.

title: Bukayo
intro: Chewy coconut candy made by cooking grated coconut in brown sugar syrup until sticky, then shaping it into small patties. It is sweet, caramel-like and full of coconut.

steps.text: Boil the sugar, water and pandan in a wide pan, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Add the grated coconut and cook over medium-low heat, stirring often, until the syrup is almost gone and the coconut is sticky and clumps together.
Remove the pandan. Drop tablespoons of the mixture onto an oiled tray or banana leaf and flatten them slightly.
Let the bukayo cool until set.

tips: Stop cooking while the mixture is still glossy: overcooked bukayo turns hard once it cools. Keeps 1 week in an airtight container.

title: Macapuno balls
intro: Soft, chewy balls of macapuno cooked with condensed milk and rolled in sugar. They taste of sweet, creamy coconut.

steps.text: Cook the macapuno, condensed milk and butter in a nonstick pan over low heat, stirring constantly, until very thick and sticky and the mixture pulls away from the pan.
Spread on a buttered plate and let it cool completely.
With buttered hands, roll teaspoons of the mixture into balls.
Roll the balls in sugar and set them in paper cups or wrap them in cellophane.

tips: If the cooled mixture is too soft to roll, chill it for 30 minutes first. Keep in the fridge for up to 1 week.

title: Bandi
intro: Peanut brittle made with muscovado, so it is darker and deeper in flavor than one made with white sugar. It is crunchy, toasty and not too sweet.

steps.text: Toast the peanuts in a dry pan over medium-low heat, stirring, until golden and their skins blister. Set them aside.
Oil a baking tray or line it with banana leaf.
In the same pan, stir the sugar and water over medium heat until dissolved, then boil without stirring until thick and dark and a drop in cold water turns hard and brittle.
Quickly stir in the peanuts, butter and salt, then pour onto the tray and spread thin with an oiled spatula.
Score into pieces while still warm, then let it cool until hard and break along the lines.

tips: Work fast once the peanuts go in, because the syrup sets within a minute. Store airtight: humid air makes brittle sticky.

title: Sampalok candy
intro: Ripe tamarind pulp cooked with sugar and a pinch of salt, rolled into balls and coated in sugar. It is sweet, sour and salty all at once.

steps.text: Peel the tamarind pods and pull off the stringy fibers.
Soak the pulp in the hot water until soft.
Squeeze and press the pulp with your fingers to free the seeds, and discard them.
Cook the pulp with 1 cup sugar and the salt in a nonstick pan over low heat, stirring, until it becomes a thick paste that pulls away from the pan.
Let the paste cool.
Roll into 2-cm balls and coat them in the remaining sugar.

tips: Sour tamarind may need a little more sugar; taste the paste before it cools. Add a pinch of chili flakes for the spicy version. Store airtight for up to 2 weeks.

title: Banana con yelo
intro: Caramelized saba bananas in their syrup, topped with shaved ice and cold evaporated milk. It is sweet, creamy and icy, a simple afternoon cooler.

steps.text: Cook the saba, sugar and water in a pan over medium heat, stirring gently, until the bananas are tender and coated in a thick, dark syrup.
Let it cool, then chill until cold.
Divide the bananas and syrup among 4 glasses.
Pack the shaved ice on top, pour 0.25 cup evaporated milk over each and serve with long spoons.

tips: Cook the bananas the day before and keep them in the fridge. A sprinkle of pinipig or a scoop of vanilla ice cream on top makes it a treat.

title: Mais con yelo
intro: Sweet corn kernels with sugar, shaved ice and cold milk, topped with crisp pinipig. It is creamy, icy and tastes of summer corn.

items.name: sweet corn kernels
items.note: from 3 boiled ears, or canned and drained

steps.text: If using fresh corn, boil the ears until tender, let them cool, then cut off the kernels. Chill the corn.
Put 0.5 cup corn and 1 tablespoon sugar in each glass and stir.
Pack the shaved ice on top and pour 0.25 cup evaporated milk over each.
Sprinkle with pinipig and serve right away.

tips: Cream-style corn works too: use 0.333 cup per glass and skip half the sugar. Add a scoop of vanilla ice cream for a richer version.

title: Guinumis
intro: Shaved ice with coconut milk, brown sugar syrup, sago, gulaman and toasted pinipig. It is cold, creamy and caramel-sweet, lighter than halo-halo.

steps.text: Boil the sago in about 6 cups water, stirring now and then, then cover off the heat until the pearls are clear. Drain and rinse.
Simmer the brown sugar and water until it turns into a light, glossy syrup. Let it cool.
Toast the pinipig in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring, until crisp and fragrant.
Spoon 2 tablespoons syrup, some sago and gulaman into each glass.
Pack shaved ice on top, pour about 0.333 cup coconut milk over each, sprinkle with pinipig and serve.

tips: Make the syrup, sago and gulaman ahead and keep them in the fridge, so all that is left is the ice. Add more syrup to taste at the table.

title: Avocado with milk
intro: Ripe avocado scooped into a glass with sugar and cold milk, lightly mashed and eaten with a spoon. It is creamy, mildly sweet and very cold.

steps.text: Halve the avocados, remove the pits and scoop the flesh into two glasses or bowls in chunks.
Sprinkle with the sugar and mash lightly with a spoon, leaving some chunks.
Pour in the milk and add the ice, then stir and eat right away with a spoon.

tips: Chill the avocados and milk an hour ahead so it is cold without too much ice. It browns quickly, so make it just before eating.

title: Graham balls
intro: Graham cracker crumbs kneaded with condensed milk, wrapped around a mini marshmallow and rolled in more crumbs. They are sweet, soft and chewy, an easy no-bake treat to make with kids.

steps.text: Mix the 2 cups crumbs and condensed milk in a bowl until it forms a firm dough that holds together.
Scoop 1 tablespoon of dough, flatten it in your palm, put a marshmallow in the center and roll it into a ball.
Roll each ball in the remaining crumbs.
Chill the balls until firm, then set them in paper cups.

tips: If the dough is too sticky, add a spoonful more crumbs; if it cracks, add a little condensed milk. Keep in the fridge for up to 5 days.

title: Chocolate graham float
intro: A no-bake icebox cake of graham crackers layered with chocolate cream and topped with grated chocolate. It chills into soft, fudgy, cake-like layers.

steps.text: Beat the cold cream in a chilled bowl until thickened.
Add the condensed milk and cocoa and beat until smooth and evenly brown.
Cover the bottom of a 9 x 13-inch dish with graham crackers and spread a layer of chocolate cream over them.
Repeat the layers 3 or 4 times, ending with cream.
Cover the top with grated chocolate.
Cover and chill for at least 6 hours before slicing.

tips: Overnight chilling gives the softest, most cake-like layers. Sliced bananas between the layers are a good addition.

title: Mango graham cake
intro: A round no-bake cake with a buttery graham crust, mango cream made with pureed mango, and a layer of fresh mango slices on top. It is fruity, creamy and sliced like a real cake.

steps.text: Mix the crumbs and melted butter and press firmly into the bottom of an 8-inch springform pan. Chill while you make the filling.
Puree 1 mango until smooth; you need about 1 cup. Slice the other 2 mangoes thinly.
Beat the cold cream until thickened, then beat in the condensed milk and fold in the mango puree.
Spread half the mango cream over the crust and cover it with a layer of whole graham crackers, breaking them to fit.
Add half the mango slices, then the rest of the cream. Arrange the remaining slices on top.
Freeze for at least 4 hours until firm enough to slice, then release the springform and let it soften for 10 minutes before cutting.

tips: Freezing gives the cleanest slices; you can also chill it overnight instead for a softer cake. Keep leftovers in the freezer for up to 1 week.

title: No-bake ube cheesecake
intro: A no-bake cheesecake with a graham crust and a purple filling of cream cheese and ube halaya, swirled with more halaya on top. It is creamy, a little tangy and tastes of sweet ube.

steps.text: Mix the crumbs and melted butter and press firmly into an 8-inch springform pan. Chill while you make the filling.
Beat the cream cheese until completely smooth, then beat in 1 cup ube halaya, the condensed milk and the flavoring.
In another bowl, whip the cream to soft peaks and fold it gently into the ube mixture.
Pour the filling over the crust and smooth the top.
Loosen the remaining 0.5 cup halaya with the milk, dot it over the top and swirl with a knife.
Cover and chill for at least 6 hours, until set, before releasing the pan and slicing.

tips: Chill it overnight for the firmest slices, and wipe the knife between cuts. Keeps 4 days in the fridge.

title: Mango ice cream
intro: A no-churn ice cream of whipped cream, condensed milk and ripe mango puree, with bits of mango through it. It is creamy, fruity and needs no machine.

steps.text: Puree 2 mangoes until smooth; you need about 2 cups. Dice the third mango.
Whip the cream in a cold bowl until it holds stiff peaks.
Stir the condensed milk into the mango puree, then fold this gently into the whipped cream until no streaks remain. Fold in the diced mango.
Spread in a loaf pan, cover tightly and freeze for at least 6 hours, until firm.
Let it soften for 5 minutes before scooping.

tips: All-purpose cream does not whip as stiffly as whipping cream, so the ice cream will be denser but still good. Keeps 2 weeks in the freezer, covered.

title: Ube macapuno ice cream
intro: A no-churn purple ice cream made with ube halaya, with chewy strings of macapuno folded through. It is creamy and sweet, with an earthy ube flavor and bits of soft coconut.

steps.text: Beat the ube halaya, condensed milk and flavoring together until smooth.
Whip the cream in a cold bowl until it holds stiff peaks.
Fold the ube mixture into the whipped cream until evenly purple.
Spread a third in a loaf pan, scatter over a third of the macapuno and repeat twice.
Cover tightly and freeze for at least 6 hours, until firm. Soften for 5 minutes before scooping.

tips: Use firm, thick halaya; a runny one makes icy ice cream. Keeps 2 weeks in the freezer.

title: Cheese ice cream
intro: A no-churn ice cream made with processed cheddar, half melted into the base and half grated through it. It is sweet and slightly salty, with soft bits of cheese.

steps.text: Warm the evaporated milk in a small pan over low heat, add half the cheese and stir until melted and smooth.
Stir in the condensed milk and let the mixture cool completely.
Whip the cream in a cold bowl until it holds stiff peaks.
Fold the cheese mixture into the cream, then fold in the rest of the grated cheese.
Spread in a loaf pan, cover tightly and freeze for at least 6 hours. Soften for 5 minutes before scooping.

tips: Processed cheddar (the kind sold in a box) gives the classic flavor and stays soft when frozen; aged cheddar turns hard and crumbly. Keeps 2 weeks in the freezer.

title: Avocado ice cream
intro: A pale green no-churn ice cream of ripe avocado, condensed milk and whipped cream. It is rich, buttery and smooth, like a frozen avocado with milk.

steps.text: Blend the avocado, condensed milk and calamansi juice until completely smooth.
Whip the cream in a cold bowl until it holds stiff peaks.
Fold the avocado mixture into the cream until no streaks remain.
Spread in a loaf pan, press plastic wrap on the surface and freeze for at least 6 hours.
Soften for 5 minutes before scooping.

tips: Use avocados that are ripe but not brown inside. Plastic wrap pressed on the surface keeps the top from darkening. Best eaten within 1 week.

title: Minatamis na pulang munggo
intro: Red mung beans simmered until soft, then cooked in brown sugar until glossy. They are sweet and creamy inside, a must for halo-halo and good over shaved ice with milk.

steps.text: Bring the beans and water to a boil in a pot, then simmer covered until the beans are soft but still whole, adding hot water if they get dry.
Add the sugar and salt and simmer uncovered over low heat, stirring gently, until the syrup is thick and glossy.
Let the beans cool in their syrup.
Spoon into clean jars and refrigerate.

tips: Soak the beans overnight to cut the simmering time roughly in half. Add the sugar only once the beans are soft, or they stay hard. Keeps 2 weeks in the fridge.

title: Macaroni fruit salad
intro: Elbow macaroni and fruit cocktail folded into sweet cream and condensed milk with cheese cubes and raisins. It is creamy and sweet with a soft chew from the pasta, a Christmas party favorite.

steps.text: Cook the macaroni in salted boiling water until just tender, a minute past the package time.
Drain, rinse under cold water until cool and drain very well.
Stir the cream and condensed milk together in a large bowl.
Fold in the macaroni, fruit cocktail, cheese, raisins and nata de coco.
Cover and chill for at least 2 hours before serving.

tips: The pasta soaks up the dressing as it sits, so keep a little extra cream to stir in before serving. Eat within 2 days.
